content.title: Real Madrid 3 Atletico Madrid 2 – How good was Molina’s goal? Why was Valverde sent off?
content.text: Meetings between Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid seldom let you down on the entertainment front — and Sunday’s La Liga meeting at the Bernabeu was another wild rollercoaster.Ademola Lookman gave Atletico the lead in the 33rd minute, finishing from close range after a Giuliano Simeone flick unlocked the home defence on the counter-attack, leaving stand-in goalkeeper Andriy Lunin with no chance.But in three early second-half minutes, the home side totally turned the tie around. First, Vinicius Junior’s 52nd-minute penalty brought them level after David Hancko’s clumsy challenge on Brahim Diaz. Three minutes later, Federico Valverde stole the ball from Jose Maria Gimenez on the edge of the box and poked the ball beyond goalkeeper Juan Musso.With half an hour to play, on came Kylian Mbappe and Trent Alexander-Arnold — the latter had been left out of the starting XI after being late for training. They were soon witnesses to a 66th-minute Nahuel Molina wonderstrike that brought Atletico level at 2-2. Five minutes later, though, Madrid were in front again, Vinicius Jr adding his second of the night as he swept home with aplomb from the edge of the box, having been set up by Alexander-Arnold’s driving run and pass.Jude Bellingham then made his return from injury in the Madrid midfield — and shortly after the home side were reduced to 10, with Valverde sent off in the 77th minute for a challenge on Alex Baena — two players who have history. As Atletico pressed for another equaliser, Julian Alvarez hit the post with a shot from outside the box, but Madrid managed to hang on for an important win.The result means they stay four points behind defending champions Barcelona, who lead the Spanish table.Here, The Athletic’s Dermot Corrigan breaks down the major talking points.How good was Molina’s goal?Atletico started brightly and probably had the better of the first half. They might even have had a penalty after a Dani Carvajal slide on Marcos Llorente in the box after the Atletico right-back saw a close-range shot well saved by Lunin, who was replacing the injured Thibaut Courtois.But the key moment of the half came when Lookman picked up possession in space deep inside the Madrid half, with his marker Carvajal having been distracted by Antoine Griezmann’s off-the-ball run.Lookman fed overlapping left-back Matteo Ruggieri down the wing, and from the Italian’s cross, a neat flick by Simeone, Atletico manager Diego’s son, found the one-time Everton winger in space. He calmly placed the ball past Lunin for the opener, making it five goals and four assists in his first 14 games since joining from Atalanta of Italy for an initial €35million (£30.3m/$40.4m at the current rates) on deadline day in February.It was a really neat passing move by Atletico — but Molina’s goal for their second was even better.Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesAfter Madrid had managed to claw themselves into a winning position, the 27-year-old right-back struck a fierce drive from outside the box that arrowed right into the top corner.It was the kind of goal that deserves to win a match — unfortunately for Diego Simeone’s side, that wasn’t the case here.How did Madrid take control?Atletico would have expected to do plenty of defending to hold onto their lead after half-time, but instead they meekly gave it up.First, Diaz dribbled into the area and tempted Hancko into a rash challenge that the Slovakia international defender really did not have to make. Hancko possibly got a touch on the ball, but he also caught Brahim. Referee Jose Luis Munuera Montero pointed to the spot and there was no way his call was going to be overturned by the VAR team.Vinicius Jr has had a rocky time on penalties this season, missing two of six previously, but on this occasion the Brazilian nervelessly slammed his shot into the net to make it 1-1.Just three minutes later came more self-destruction from Atletico. Ruggieri’s pass inside was slightly underhit but while Valverde is super-athletic, Gimenez really should have cleared the ball.Javier Soriano/AFP via Getty ImagesInstead, Gimenez’s challenge was too weak, and Valverde was able to burst past an opponent who is his team-mate for the Uruguayan national team. He then slid the ball confidently beyond Musso to complete the turnaround.Two mistakes from Atletico had been ruthlessly punished by Madrid, but the goal that turned out to be the winner on the night was a moment of real quality. After Molina’s tremendous piledriver levelled the scores again, Vinicius Jr replied with his own fine strike, taking a pass from substitute Alexander-Arnold and coming inside to curl a right footer from the edge of the area low into the far corner.After just one goal in his first 19 ‘derbis’ against Atletico, he had scored two in 20 minutes.Why was Valverde sent off?Perhaps the biggest talking point in the game came when Valverde had a hack at Atletico substitute Baena in midfield. The referee was sure and immediately whipped out his red card.It was a strong challenge, definitely a foul, but sending Valverde off seemed harsh. Among those to protest strongly was Madrid head coach Alvaro Arbeloa but the VAR officials did not recommend a change of decision and the home team were down to 10.Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesMany viewers, and presumably all involved, would have recalled the history between Valverde and Baena, around another game at the Bernabeu in April 2023, when the latter was a Villarreal player.After an exchange of words between the pair on the pitch, Valverde was alleged to have waited for Baena in the stadium car park and then punched him in the face. The Spaniard filed a police complaint over the incident but it was dismissed.What next for Real Madrid?Saturday, April 4: Mallorca (Away), La Liga, 3.15pm UK, 10.15am ETWhat next for Atletico Madrid?Saturday, April 4: Barcelona (Home), La Liga, 8pm UK, 3pm ET
